entries: Lawn work | Mowing and edging | Mow or edge lawns using power mowers or edgers; mulch, aerate, weed, grub, and dethatch established lawns, or edge along flower beds, walks, and walls.

Trees, shrubs, and flowers | Pruning and shaping | Prune or shape trees, shrubs, or hedges using pruning shears or chain saws; trim or pick flowers, clean flower beds, and attach planted trees to support stakes.

Planting and landscaping | Design and planting | Follow established landscape designs to determine where to lay sod, sow seeds, and plant flowers and greenery. Plant using gardening tools, apply protective mulch, transport or spread topsoil, or cover ground with straw to stabilize the soil.

Irrigation, fertilization, and pesticide use | Watering and spraying | Water using portable irrigation systems, hoses, or watering cans. Mix and spray or spread fertilizers, herbicides, and insecticides using hand-held or automatic sprayers and spreaders.

Grounds and facility maintenance | Removal and upkeep | Sweep and remove litter; rake, mulch, and compost leaves; maintain walks, driveways, parking lots, fountains, planters, and other grounds features; clear snow and spread salt.

Equipment and planning | Operation and cultivation | Operate vehicles or powered equipment; maintain or repair tools, equipment, or structures using hand or power tools; care for natural turf grounds and plan or cultivate lawns or gardens.

Boundary conclusion | This page corresponds to O*NET 37-3011.00 (Landscaping and Groundskeeping Workers). The core distinction from neighboring occupations is their primary objects, outputs, and actual duties. This occupation works with lawns, trees, shrubs, flowers, ground cover, and grounds features on property, combining pruning, irrigation, fertilization, pesticide use, planting, waste removal, and facility maintenance. Outputs are maintained grounds and inspection and equipment records. First-Line Supervisors of Landscaping, Lawn Service, and Groundskeeping Workers (37-1012.00) focus on crews, work arrangements, and quality and safety supervision. Tree Trimmers and Pruners (37-3013.00) focus on specialized tree pruning and removal work at height. Pesticide Handlers, Sprayers, and Applicators, Vegetation (37-3012.00) focus on specialized pesticide and fertilizer application and pest and disease control. Highway Maintenance Workers (47-4051.00) focus on roads, roadsides, and traffic facilities. Maintenance and Repair Workers, General (49-9071.00) focus on general building and equipment maintenance and repair. Agricultural Equipment Operators (45-2091.00), Fallers (45-4021.00), and Farmworkers and Laborers, Crop, Nursery, and Greenhouse (45-2092.00) work in agricultural production and forestry operations. Helpers—Pipelayers, Plumbers, Pipefitters, and Steamfitters (47-3015.00) and Operating Engineers and Other Construction Equipment Operators (47-2073.00) work with pipelines, earthworks, and construction machinery. Their objects, operations, and authorization levels differ; authority to determine plant health and pests or diseases, devise pesticide and fertilizer plans, assess grounds structures and safety, or reach environmental compliance conclusions cannot be carried across occupations.
